verses.text: Jesus went into the synagogue again. A man with a shriveled hand was there.
Some people watched Jesus closely, ready to accuse him, just to see whether he’d heal the man on the Sabbath.
Jesus told the man with the shriveled hand, “Stand up here where everyone can see.”
Then he asked them, “On the Sabbath, is it right to do good or do harm—to save a life or destroy one?” They stayed quiet.
Jesus looked around at them, angry and deeply grieved because their hearts were so hard. Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored.
The Pharisees went out and immediately started plotting with the supporters of Herod about how to kill Jesus.
Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea. A huge crowd followed from Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem,
from Idumea, the far side of the Jordan, and the areas around Tyre and Sidon. They’d heard what he was doing, so crowds came through.
Jesus told his disciples to keep a small boat ready in case the crowd crushed in on him.
He had healed so many that everyone with an illness pushed forward, trying to touch him.
Whenever unclean spirits saw him, they fell down in front of him and shouted, “You are the Son of God!”
But Jesus firmly warned them not to tell people who he was.
Jesus went up the mountain and called over the people he wanted. They came to him.
He appointed twelve to stay with him, sent them out to preach,
and gave them authority to cast out demons.
He named Simon “Peter,”
James son of Zebedee and his brother John—he named them Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder,”
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who later betrayed him. Then Jesus went into a house.
The crowd gathered again, so packed that Jesus and his disciples couldn’t even eat.
When his family heard about it, they went out to take charge of him. People were saying, “He’s out of his mind.”
The legal teachers who had come down from Jerusalem said, “He’s got Beelzebul!” and, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
Jesus called them over and answered with a story: “How can Satan drive Satan out?
“If a kingdom is split against itself, that kingdom can’t stand.
“And if a household is split against itself, that household can’t stand.
“So if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he can’t stand—his end has come.
“Nobody can break into a strong man’s house and steal his stuff unless they first tie up the strong man. Then they can clear out his house.
“I’m telling you the truth: people can be forgiven for every sin and for all the slander they speak.
“But whoever slanders the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; that sin lasts forever.”
He said this because they were claiming, “He has an unclean spirit.”
Then Jesus’ mother and brothers arrived. They stood outside and sent someone in to call him.
A crowd was sitting around him. They told him, “Your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.”
He answered, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
He looked around at the people sitting there and said, “Here are my mother and my brothers!
“Whoever does God’s will is my brother, my sister, and my mother.”
